name: API contract check
description: After a controller or API DTO is saved, check the change against the API conventions and keep docs/api.md consistent.

action.prompt:
A controller or request/response record under an api package was saved. Review only the saved file and the endpoints it defines.

Check against .kiro/steering/architecture.md (API conventions) and the design.md of the owning spec in .kiro/specs/:
- Path, HTTP method, status codes (201 with Location on create, 202 on simulation submit, 404, 409, 422) match the spec.
- The controller is thin: no repository use, no business logic, no JPA entity in any signature. Types are *Request / *Response records.
- Every request body is annotated @Valid and its fields carry Bean Validation constraints matching the spec's limits.
- List endpoints return the standard envelope (items, page, size, totalItems, totalPages), accept factoryId, and cap size at 200.
- Decimal quantities and money are serialised as strings; timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC; durations are integer seconds with the unit in the field name; result objects carry source ACTUAL or SIMULATED.
- Errors go through the central problem+json advice; nothing in the controller builds an error body or exposes exception details.
- OpenAPI annotations (summary and response codes) are present.

Then compare with docs/api.md: if an endpoint, field or status code in the saved file differs from what docs/api.md says, update docs/api.md in the same change. If the saved file adds an endpoint that is not in the owning spec's design.md, stop and report it instead of documenting it: the spec must be updated first.

Report only discrepancies found and edits made. If everything is consistent, say so in one line. Do not start the application to fetch /v3/api-docs unless asked.
